title: Deterministic \(\widetilde O(n^{5/2})\) worst-case dynamic APSP
formal: Is there a deterministic fully dynamic exact all-pairs distance structure on a fixed universe of \(N\) vertex labels, for directed real-weighted graphs with no negative directed cycle, with polynomial initialization, \(O(N^2\log^c(2+N))\) space, \(O(N^{5/2}\log^c(2+N))\) worst-case time per vertex insertion or deletion, and O(1) time per distance query, for an absolute constant c?
definitions:
At any time a subset of \([N]\) is active. Inserting an inactive label supplies all incoming and outgoing edges between it and currently active vertices, with their finite real weights; at most \(2(N-1)\) such entries are supplied. Deleting an active label removes it and all incident edges. Graphs are simple as directed graphs, though both opposite arcs may exist. Every resulting graph is promised to have no negative directed cycle. The structure is not required to detect a violated promise.

For active u,v, a query returns the exact minimum weight of a directed u-to-v path, infinity if none exists, and zero for u=v. The no-negative-cycle promise makes every finite minimum well defined even with negative edges. Reporting a path is not required. Query arguments always refer to active labels.

Use a uniform random-access arithmetic machine with exact addition, subtraction and comparison of real weights and word arithmetic on \(\Theta(\log N)\)-bit identifiers and addresses. Each arithmetic, comparison or memory operation costs one. One weight occupies one cell, without arbitrary packing and decoding of many weights. All retained data, including the current graph, count toward space. Input-reading cost for each supplied incident-edge list is included.

The initial graph may be preprocessed in \(N^{O(1)}\) operations. Thereafter each individual update must satisfy the stated bound, over all legal histories, with no amortization or randomness. The resource parameter N is a fixed maximum universe size, not the fluctuating number of active vertices. Deleting and reinserting a vertex may replace many incident weights, but a vertex operation must not be confused with a single-edge operation.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked algorithm and proof of exact query answers and all resource bounds, or a Lean-checked refutation in the stated model. A randomized algorithm with high-probability correctness, an amortized update theorem, or a different update granularity is insufficient. Any conditional barrier must be explicitly conditional.
context:
Mao obtains the stated near-quadratic space and approximately N^(5/2) worst-case vertex-update bound using a Monte Carlo algorithm. The paper treats graphs without negative cycles and explicitly contrasts the deterministic frontier.

The catalogue target asks to remove randomness while retaining that combination of resources. Earlier near-quadratic amortized maintenance and randomized worst-case maintenance do not provide deterministic guarantees on every update.
why: This isolates the cost of removing randomness from a central worst-case dynamic shortest-path bound.

import_provenance.original_title: Derandomizing the n^{5/2} worst-case dynamic APSP bound
import_provenance.original_statement: Maintain exact distances in a directed weighted graph under insertion or deletion of a vertex and its incident edges, with constant-time distance queries and Õ(n²) space. Can deterministic worst-case update time match the Õ(n^{5/2}) randomized bound?
import_provenance.supplied_caveat: Remark: The Õ(n²) amortized update target and the randomized Õ(n^{5/2}) worst-case target are already achieved. This is the deterministic worst-case strengthening, for graphs with no negative cycles.

The catalogue target asks to remove randomness while retaining that combination of resources. Earlier near-quadratic amortized maintenance and randomized worst-case maintenance do not provide deterministic guarantees on every update.

sentences: The graph changes by inserting or deleting an entire vertex and its incident edges.
Queries ask for exact directed distances under a no-negative-cycle promise.
The target combines deterministic N^(5/2) worst-case updates with near-quadratic storage and constant queries.
The checked matching-exponent result is randomized, and amortized results provide a different guarantee.
This isolates the cost of determinism in exact dynamic shortest paths.
